I've finished cross-checking the 2024 year-end balances against the 2025 distributions. Here's what I found.

**Yes. All three 2025 required minimum distributions were taken in full, from accounts allowed to pay them, before the 1 April 2026 deadline.**

**Who owed RMDs.** Prema Raghavan (born 1952-07-22) turned 73 in 2025, so 2025 was her first RMD year and the deadline was 1 April 2026. All three of her retirement accounts owed one: two traditional IRAs and the Hollins and Reade 401(k). She retired from that employer in 2020, so the "still working" exception doesn't apply. Martin Kessler is 68 and owns no retirement accounts here, and the joint account is taxable.

**Divisor.** Martin is her sole beneficiary on all three accounts, but he is less than 10 years younger. That means the Uniform Lifetime Table applies, with a factor of 26.5 at age 73.

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 balance (positions + cash) | 2025 RMD | Taken (gross) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SYN-58140002 IRA | $582,446.94 | $21,979.13 | $29,329.16 on 2025-12-04 | Covers both IRAs |
| SYN-58140003 IRA | $194,775.76 | $7,350.03 | none | Covered by 0002 |
| SYN-58140004 401(k) | $311,957.24 | $11,771.97 | $11,771.97 on 2025-11-05 | Met |

- **IRAs:** You can add together the RMDs of one person's IRAs and take the total from any of them. $21,979.13 + $7,350.03 = $29,329.16, which exactly matches the single distribution from SYN-58140002. This follows the instruction she signed on 2025-11-24 and matches that account's 1099-R.
- **401(k):** A 401(k) RMD can't be combined with the IRAs and has to come from the plan itself. It did, to the cent, matching both the plan's 1099-R and her instruction of 2025-10-27.
- **Withholding:** The 10% federal tax withheld is part of the gross distribution, so it counts toward the RMD.
- **Cross-check:** The Q1 2026 statement for SYN-58140002 matches the custodian's positions and cash at 2026-03-31.
- **Not reviewed:** I didn't review fees or allocation against the investment policy, because the question doesn't depend on them.

**Follow-up:** Her 2026 RMDs are due by 31 December 2026, based on the 31 Dec 2025 balances. The records show no 2026 distribution as of 15 April 2026.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds one client household's records as they stood on 15 April 2026: the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/), its CRM (crm/) and the statements and tax forms on file (documents/).

The advisor asks: was every 2025 required minimum distribution from this household's retirement accounts taken, from the right accounts, by 1 April 2026?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "rmd_missed" if any 2025 required minimum distribution was not taken in full, from the accounts it had to come from, by its deadline; "all_rmds_met" if every one was; or "unresolved"
- "rmds": one entry per account that owes a 2025 required minimum distribution, each as {"account_id": ..., "rmd": its 2025 required minimum distribution}
- "missed": one entry per required minimum distribution not met, each as {"account_ids": the accounts it had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken}, or [] if none
- "total_shortfall": the shortfalls added up, 0 if none, or null if unresolved
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read; cite a factor from the IRS life-expectancy tables with "source": "IRS Publication 590-B"
- "explanation": two or three sentences
